absent: CPU sync try get path, owner and nesting variable definitions, and full acquire release protocol beyond the put side.
Ring core operations reserve commit read init and helpers for last finalized, valid read, record init, plus descriptor and data ring sizing macros and block position encoding.
Meanings of printk info flag bits, caller id selection, execution context gating, task name length, and device info layout.
Kunit, thread, timer, wait queue, cpumask, and scheduling helper semantics beyond names cited as stubs.
Backing variables for console loglevel, ratelimit state, delay, devkmsg string, dmesg restrict, and pointer restrict, and their allowed value semantics.
Static call key site mod struct layouts, address and flag helpers, architecture transform, module site ranges, system and module states, and sort implementation.

findings.text: Provides a release operation for printk per CPU synchronization ownership. It handles a nesting count first and otherwise publishes vacancy with release ordering so earlier accesses become visible to the next acquirer.

Release side of a pairing where put publishes vacancy with release semantics and the matching try get side is expected to acquire. The description states that observing vacancy implies visibility of prior loads and stores from the previous owner.
If the nesting counter is nonzero on entry the operation only decrements it and returns without changing ownership. Only a zero nesting value proceeds to publish release.

Ring sizing helpers derive index masks by subtracting one from the associated capacity, one for the data area and one for the descriptor count. This implies power of two capacities with wrapping offsets.
Variable length data element holding a numeric identifier followed by trailing payload bytes. Payload extent is determined by surrounding ring bookkeeping rather than a length inside this header.

Exposes a helper returning the sequence number expected after the last finalized record. It starts from the last finalized value, adjusts for the bootstrap zero case, then advances while a valid record exists at the candidate.

When last finalized sequence is nonzero the search begins at its successor, otherwise it begins at zero because bootstrap presence at index zero is uncertain. Finalized information is treated as possibly stale so forward scanning corrects it.

Record metadata carrying sequence and timestamp, text length, syslog facility, split bitfields for internal flags and level, caller identifiers with optional complement and task name when execution context is enabled, plus embedded device specific info.
Transfer object pairing a metadata pointer with a text buffer pointer and its capacity. It decouples descriptor state from payload movement between writers and readers.
Data block position pair holding begin and next logical positions. Together they delimit one stored text extent inside the data ring.
Descriptor coupling an atomic state word with the position pair for its associated text block. State moves atomically while block positions describe payload linkage.
Text storage management with size expressed as bits, a byte pointer to storage, and atomic head and tail logical positions for allocation and reclamation.
Descriptor management with count as bits, pointers to descriptor and info arrays, and atomic head and tail identifiers plus last finalized sequence for reader progress.
Top level ring combining a descriptor ring, a text data ring, and an atomic failure counter. Coordination relies on the subring atomics.
Reservation handle retaining the ring pointer, saved interrupt flags, descriptor identifier, and amount of text space granted. It links reserve and commit phases for one writer.

Descriptor lifecycle uses reserved for writer owned, committed for writer finished but reopenable, finalized for immutable, reusable for free, plus a negative miss pseudo value for identifier mismatch on read paths.

Size helper raises two to a bit count. State width equals machine word width with top two bits as flags, shift derived from width, mask covering those bits, and identifier occupying low bits via complement mask.
Sentinel logical positions use value one for failed and three for empty line, with a combined initializer setting both begin and next to failed to denote no associated block.

Static ring construction presets the last descriptor as reusable with failed block linkage and presets info entries so first reservation advances to zero while bootstrap reports zero. Head and tail identifiers start at the initial descriptor and data positions start at the initial block, with text bits as sum of descriptor and average text bits and failure count zero.
Convenience macro allocates static text storage sized as two raised to the sum of descriptor and average text bits, aligned to word boundary, then delegates to the fuller initializer.
Header uses a conventional include guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.
Test defaults to a ten second run. Test payload caps text at hex eighty bytes and record size as header plus that cap.

Test scaffolding defines a sized payload with counted trailing text, a shared context with test pointer ring pointer and wait queue, per thread context with numeric id and shared pointer, and a timer plus task pairing for timed wakeup.
Payload validation requires size at least two and within cap, trailing zero terminator, and all preceding bytes equal to the first byte. Failures are reported with sequence size and text.

Writer threads loop choosing a random text size in range, initializing a write record, attempting reservation and on success filling length and payload with a repeated per thread character plus terminator, committing, waking readers, periodically yielding, until stop is requested.

Reader installs a one shot timer that flags and wakes the current task, then waits for each sequence to become valid, checks monotonicity and payload integrity, yields periodically, advances to successor, and finally tears down the timer.

Kunit case builds a small test ring, snapshots online CPUs, reserves one CPU for the reader and starts a writer on each remaining CPU, pins itself to the reader CPU, runs the reader for the configured duration, and registers cleanup for masks and threads under a suite for the printk ringbuffer.

Under full load reservation may fail when no descriptor is free or the oldest record is still reserved. The stress test intentionally ignores such failures to focus on races and consistency. Reader treats a read sequence below expectation as failure.
A global atomic counter tracks forced console requests, incremented on enter and decremented on exit, allowing nesting.
Per CPU integer records safe nesting depth, incremented on safe enter and decremented on safe exit. Deferred variants additionally assert non migratability around the same accounting.

Legacy deferred decision is true when forced legacy kthread mode holds, or safe nesting is nonzero, or execution is in non maskable interrupt context, or the current CPU owns the printk CPU synchronization. The per CPU depth is described as safe to read anywhere because migration is disabled while set.
Upper bound constant for delay control equals ten thousand.
A sysctl handler for privileged knobs denies writes without administrator capability and otherwise delegates to the bounded integer vector handler.

Sysctl table exposes printk levels, ratelimit interval and burst, delay bounded between zero and ten thousand, devkmsg string control, and two administrator gated controls for dmesg restriction and pointer restriction with ranges zero to one and zero to two respectively, all with owner write and world read permissions.
Provides a generic helper returning zero as a long, usable as a default static call target.
Global integer records whether static call patching is initialized. Force reinit warns when not initialized and otherwise increments the generation to trigger reprocessing.
A dedicated mutex serializes static call updates through small lock and unlock wrappers held across key modification and site patching.

Key extraction masks low flag bits from the encoded site key. Tail detection tests a tail flag, init marking sets an init flag with relative adjustment, and type low bit distinguishes inline site list versus module list with accessors returning either sites or mods.

Site ordering compares owning keys by address, swaps entries while adjusting relative address and key offsets by the displacement between slots, and sorts a contiguous site range with those callbacks.

Update path takes CPU read protection and the static call mutex, ignores requests that do not change the function, publishes the new function and patches the trampoline, then walks core and module site lists patching each site belonging to the key while skipping init sites after boot, skipping non kernel text sites with a one time warning, and honouring tail versus non tail transformation.

Patching is skipped entirely when not initialized beyond the trampoline, with a one time warning. Sites without associated storage, such as keys defined but unused in a module or the synthetic first entry in moded keys, are ignored. Early boot versus module coming state selects whether init sites are eligible.
